Resin or rubber

Resin bound surfacing

Stone aggregate mixed with resin and laid smooth. The surface is porous, so water drains through it.

It is often used on driveways and paths.

Rubber surfacing

Rubber granules, often recycled, bound together with polyurethane. The surface is soft and slip resistant underfoot.

It is often used on playgrounds and running tracks.

Rubber on play areas and tracks.

Quick answers

Which surface suits my job?

Rubber is soft underfoot and usually suits play areas and tracks. Resin bound stone is firm and smooth and usually suits driveways and paths. If you are unsure, pick Not sure yet in the form.

Why does the base underneath matter?

Both surfaces are laid over a base. A soft or uneven base usually shows through the surface on top, so what is under it now matters.

What is the difference between resin bound and resin bonded?

In resin bonded work the stones are scattered onto a layer of resin, so the surface is rougher and water does not drain through it. In resin bound work the stone is mixed into the resin first, so the surface is smooth and porous.

What to have ready for a quote

Have these when you call or fill in the form.

  • The address or area
  • A rough size
  • What the surface is now
  • A few photos
